prompt: A classifier needs a fixed-size input but clips have different lengths. Which option solves this?
options: zero-pad every clip to the longest clip and ignore the problem of silence
summarise frame features over time (e.g. mean and standard deviation) or use global pooling
use a different sampling rate per clip
discard all clips shorter than average
explanation: Mean/std over time or global pooling gives a vector whose size does not depend on the number of frames.

prompt: Cosine k-NN predicts the label by...
options: averaging the labels of all training clips
fitting a linear boundary by gradient descent
a majority vote among the $k$ training clips with highest cosine similarity
choosing the class with the largest mean feature
explanation: k-NN has no training: it stores examples, ranks them by similarity to the query and votes.

prompt: A 3x3 convolution with padding 1 and stride 1 is applied to an input of length 100. What is the output length?
How many parameters does a Conv2d layer with 32 input channels, 64 output channels and a 3x3 kernel have (including biases)?
A model answers 'negative' for every clip in a test set with 95 negatives and 5 positives. Which statement is true?
options: accuracy 0.95 and macro F1 about 0.49
accuracy 0.50 and macro F1 0.50
accuracy 0.95 and macro F1 0.95
accuracy 1.0 and macro F1 1.0
explanation: Accuracy is $95/100$. F1 is $0.974$ for the negative class and $0$ for the positive class, so macro F1 $=0.487$.

prompt: A class has 10 true clips; the model finds 6 of them and also labels 2 clips of other classes as this class. What is its precision? (Give a decimal.)

options: it shifts the pitch of the waveform by random semitones
it masks random time and frequency bands of the log-mel spectrogram
it adds a second microphone channel
it resamples the audio at a random rate
explanation: Random frequency bands and time spans are replaced by a constant, so the network must not depend on any single patch.

prompt: Which augmentation is the worst choice for identifying a song from a short recording (Shazam-style)?
options: adding background noise
a time shift
a change of volume
a pitch shift
explanation: The pitch pattern is the identifying information; an augmentation must not change the information used for supervision.

prompt: Clips cut from the same long recording appear in both the training and test sets. The usual consequence is...
options: an overly optimistic test score because the model can recognise the recording
an overly pessimistic test score
no effect, since clips are different
a crash during training
explanation: The test clips are not independent of the training clips, so the score no longer estimates performance on new recordings.
